title: Present Church means present pastors
source_text: XXXI. Pontificii vero per Ecclesiam praesentem intelligunt uniuscujusque saeculi. Nec adhuc per illam Ecclesiam praesentem communitatem fidelium uno eodemque saeculo viventium intelligunt: sed restringunt Ecclesiae nomen ad praepositos & Pastores Ecclesiae. Itaque, quum pertendunt Scripturae authoritatem ab authoritate Ecclesiae pendere, mens eorum est, fidem illam, qua fidelis populus Scripturae libros amplectitur ut veros & divinos, niti testimonio Pastorum qui tum Ecclesiae praesunt, & testimonio illi acquiescere. Et hoc quia in Pastoribus & praesulibus Ecclesiae perpetuo residet infallibilis & divina quaedam authoritas, ex qua de libri alicujus veritate & divinitate pronunciare possint: ita ut sententia & judicium illorum fidem nostram obliget. Imo illos ea esse praeditos potestate, ut liber, qui hactenus dubiae fuit authoritatis, & de quo in utramque partem opinari licuit, per determinationem illorum fiat authenticus, & eodem postea debeat haberi numero quo libri alii sacri & canonici.
pass_a_gloss: But the Pontificians by the present Church understand [the Church] of each age. Nor do they yet by that present Church understand the community of the faithful living in one and the same age: but they restrict the name of the Church to the overseers and Pastors of the Church. Therefore, when they contend that the authority of Scripture depends on the authority of the Church, their mind is that that faith by which the faithful people embrace the books of Scripture as true and divine rests on the testimony of the Pastors who then preside over the Church, and acquiesces in that testimony. And this because in the Pastors and prelates of the Church there perpetually resides a certain infallible and divine authority, from which they can pronounce concerning the truth and divinity of any book: so that their sentence and judgment binds our faith. Indeed [they hold] that they are endowed with that power, that a book which hitherto was of doubtful authority, and about which it was permitted to opine on either side, by their determination becomes authentic, and afterwards ought to be held in the same number as the other sacred and canonical books.
pass_b_english: But by "present Church" the Pontificians mean the Church of each age.
Even then they do not mean the community of the faithful living in one and the same age. They restrict the name "Church" to the overseers and pastors of the Church.

So when they claim that the authority of Scripture depends on the authority of the Church, they mean that the faith by which the faithful people receive the books of Scripture as true and divine rests on the testimony of the pastors then in office, and settles on that testimony.

Why? Because in the pastors and prelates of the Church there always resides a certain infallible, divine authority by which they can decide the truth and divinity of a book, so that their sentence and judgment bind our faith.

They even hold that those pastors have power to make authentic a book that until then was of doubtful authority, and about which either side might be held, so that after their determination it must be ranked with the other sacred and canonical books.
